tagline: Up a dry flood channel to a waterfall with no water.
intro: From Othello SR 17 runs north through Soap Lake and up the floor of the Lower Grand Coulee, where basalt walls rise 900 feet. At Dry Falls the coulee ends at a cliff with nothing going over it. After a short piece of US 2 at Coulee City, SR 155 follows the shore of Banks Lake, 27 miles long, to Grand Coulee and the dam, then crosses the Columbia onto the Colville Reservation and goes over Disautel Pass, 3,252 feet, down to Omak.
Ice Age floods cut the coulees, released dozens of times when an ice dam in Idaho gave way. Banks Lake fills the upper coulee now, with water pumped 280 feet up out of the Columbia.

moments.title: Dry Falls
moments.text: A cliff 3.5 miles long and 400 feet high where floodwater fell at five times the width of Niagara. It has been dry since the Columbia went back to its old bed.

moments.title: Steamboat Rock
moments.text: A basalt butte standing 800 feet over Banks Lake, nearly surrounded by water, that was an island in the diverted Columbia during the last ice age.

moments.title: Grand Coulee Dam
moments.text: The largest power station in the country by capacity, and from Memorial Day through September a free laser show is projected onto its face each night.

practical: Phone service can be limited in the remote stretches, so download maps before you go. The Dry Falls interpretive center is free, but parking requires a Discover Pass.
